entry.title: "current thread is not owner" exceptions with the standard Kafka Adapter in SAP Cloud Integration
entry.content:
Hello everyone,

We are investigating a recurring issue in SAP Cloud Integration with the standard Kafka Adapter and would greatly appreciate any insights from this community.

  • Since August 2026 we have observed intermittent failures across multiple productive integration flows.
  • No deployments or configuration changes were made prior to the first occurrences.
  • Multiple runtime nodes and several production flows are affected.

Error

com.sap.it.rt.adapter.http.api.exception.HttpResponseException:
An internal server error occurred: current thread is not owner.

Additional context

  • Errors appear sporadically; sometimes services recover without intervention.
  • We found a possibly related Apache Kafka issue: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-10902 — could this be related to the underlying OpenJDK runtime?

Question

  • Has anyone else observed similar "current thread is not owner" errors with the standard Kafka Adapter in SAP Cloud Integration?

Note: I have an open SAP support ticket for about one month now, but so far without a resolution or useful feedback.

Thank you in advance for any pointers or experiences you can share.

Best regards,

Florian

entry.title: Advanced Event Mesh Adapter - PKIX Path Building Failed During Deployment
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

We are trying to configure the Advanced Event Mesh (AEM) Adapter in SAP Integration Suite (Cloud Integration) to connect to a Solace-based event broker using the SMF/JCSMP protocol over TLS.

The adapter configuration includes:

SMF/JCSMP endpoint
Basic Authentication
Secure TLS connection (tcps)
Security Material maintained in Cloud Integration

Issue

The integration flow deployment fails with the following error:

ValidatorException: PKIX path building failed

sun.security.provider.certpath.SunCertPathBuilderException:

unable to find valid certification path to requested target

 

What has already been verified

TLS Connectivity Test can successfully reach the target host and port.
DNS resolution is working.
Firewall/network connectivity appears to be working.
Required Root CA certificates have been imported into the Cloud Integration Keystore.
Additional corporate CA certificates are already available in the tenant keystore.
The endpoint credentials and VPN configuration have been verified.
Using an internal/private hostname results in:
com.solacesystems.jcsmp.JCSMPTransportException:

Login request timeout

while using the public secure endpoint results in the PKIX error above.

Questions

Has anyone encountered a PKIX error with the Advanced Event Mesh Adapter even when the root certificates already exist in the tenant keystore?
Does the AEM Adapter use the same trust validation mechanism as the standard Cloud Integration TLS Connectivity Test?
Are there known cases where the Solace broker presents an incomplete certificate chain (missing intermediate certificates), resulting in PKIX failures?
Is there a way to determine the exact certificate or trust anchor that Cloud Integration cannot validate during adapter deployment?
Are there any SAP Notes or troubleshooting guides specifically addressing PKIX errors with the Advanced Event Mesh Adapter?
Any guidance or similar experiences would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks, Ramu..

entry.title: BTP Trial – Requested runtime location (cloudintegration) is not supported for tenant
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community,

I am facing an issue with SAP Integration Suite on a BTP Trial account. Every Cloud Integration iFlow deployment fails immediately with the following error:

<iFlow name> deployment failed. Requested runtime location (: cloudintegration) is not supported for tenant: trial2-9ig6o72o

This happens even with a minimal iFlow containing only Sender → Start → End, so it does not appear to be related to the iFlow design.

Environment

  • BTP: Trial

  • Environment: Cloud Foundry

  • Region: US10

  • API Endpoint: api.cf.us10-001.hana.ondemand.com

  • Integration Suite plan: Trial

  • Current subaccount: Trial2

  • Tenant: trial2-9ig6o72o

  • Previous tenant: 120a89f2trial

  • Cloud Integration capability: Active

  • Message Queues: Enabled

  • Process Integration Runtime:

    • Plan: integration-flow

    • Status: Creation Succeeded

Troubleshooting already performed

  1. Deleted the Integration Suite subscription/entitlement from the first subaccount.

  2. Created a completely new subaccount and subscribed to Integration Suite again.

  3. Deactivated and re-added the Cloud Integration capability.

  4. Created and deployed a minimal iFlow.

  5. Tried my original iFlow as well.

  6. Checked Settings → Runtimes.

  7. Confirmed that Monitor → Integrations and APIs loads successfully.

  8. Logged out, cleared browser cache and tried again.

However, every deployment still fails with the same runtime-location error.

I also found that this appears to match SAP KBA 3748644 – Cloud Integration iFlow Deployment Fails with “Requested runtime location (cloudintegration) is not supported for tenant.”

Could someone from the SAP Integration Suite team please confirm whether this is a known issue with the BTP Trial Cloud Integration runtime provisioning?

In particular, I would like to understand whether the cloudintegration runtime needs to be reprovisioned or corrected on the SAP side for tenant trial2-9ig6o72o.

I also noticed another SAP Community post from September 17, 2026 reporting the same error on a BTP Trial tenant.

Any guidance would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

entry.title: How should CamelHttpPath be handled between an HTTP sender and HTTP receiver?
entry.content:
In SAP Cloud Integration, my HTTPS sender uses `/salesorder/*`, and a later HTTP receiver dynamically builds its URL with `${property.salesOrder}`.

The sender creates the `CamelHttpPath` header from the wildcard path. If I do not delete that header before the outbound HTTP receiver, the sales-order value is appended a second time:

`.../SalesOrderDetails('ORDER')/ORDER`

My Groovy script only extracts the order number from `CamelHttpPath` and stores it as an exchange property.

Why does the outbound HTTP receiver reuse `CamelHttpPath` in this way? I have not previously needed to delete this header before an outbound receiver. Although deleting `CamelHttpPath` fixes the duplicate-path issue, I would like to understand why it occurs and which design pattern is recommended to prevent it in future iFlows.

entry.content:
I am trying to use an MCP server defined in Integration Suite (trial). I was hoping for a seamless integration with user authentication. When that failed, I poked around a bit. From what I saw it appears that MCP gateway is not responding correctly for enabling Protected Resource Metadata Discovery . I am no expert in this. What I saw (experiment in the picture below) was that authorization_servers (rfc9728, section 2) is token endpoint. My reading is that it should be Authorization Server Metadata rfc8414, 3.2 or OpenID Discovery Configuration. So, in case of XSUAA it should be /.well-known/openid-configuration.

 So, my assumption is that is why I could not get this to work. Would you have any thoughts about this?

Dinu

entry.title: SAP Cloud Integration (CPI) - CSRF Token Invalid (/IWBEP/CM_V4H_RUN/042)
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

I am trying to call an ABAP OData V4 service from SAP Cloud Integration using the HTTP Adapter.

Scenario

I need to perform a POST operation against the following OData V4 service.

The same flow works successfully in Postman but fails from CPI with:

GET call postman

 

 
 
POST call postman

 

JSON
 
{
 
"error": {
 
"code": "/IWBEP/CM_V4H_RUN/042",
 
"message": "CSRF token is invalid",
 
"@SAP__common.ExceptionCategory": "CSRF_Token_Missing"
 
}
 
}

Current iFlow

Plain Text
 
Content Modifier 1
 
|--> x-csrf-token = Fetch
 
Request Reply (GET)
 
Content Modifier 2
 
|
 
Groovy Script
 
 
 
Request Reply (POST)

GET Call

Header:

 
 
 
HTTP
 
x-csrf-token: Fetch
 
``

HTTP Adapter Configuration:

 
 
 
Plain Text
 
Method: GET
 
Request Headers: x-csrf-token
 
Response Headers: *

The GET response returns:

 
 
 
HTTP
 
x-csrf-token: <token>
 
set-cookie:
 
sap-usercontext=...
 
sap-XSRF_AST_367=...

My Understanding

Postman works because:

  1. GET with:

     
     
     
    HTTP
     
     
     
    x-csrf-token: Fetch

  2. Receives:

     
     
     
    HTTP
     
     
     
     
    x-csrf-token: <real token>
     
    Set-Cookie: ...

  3. POST is executed with:

     
     
     
    HTTP
     
     
     
     
    x-csrf-token: <real token>
     
    Cookie: ...

and Postman automatically maintains the HTTP session.

CPI Implementation

I found a blog/forum example suggesting: https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-q-a/calling-an-odata-v4-custom-action-from-within-an-iflow/qaq-p/14088969 

Groovy

 
Groovy
 
import com.sap.gateway.ip.core.customdev.util.Message
 
 
 
def Message processData(Message message) {
 
 
 
def headers = message.getHeaders()
 
 
 
message.setProperty("CsrfToken",
 
headers.get("x-csrf-token"))
 
 
 
message.setProperty("CookieHeader",
 
headers.get("set-cookie"))
 
return message
 
}

Content Modifier before POST

 
 
 
Plain Text
 
 
 
 
Header Name Source Type Source Value
 
------------------------------------------------
 
x-csrf-token Property CsrfToken
 
Cookie Property CookieHeader

POST HTTP Adapter

Request Headers:

 
 
 
Plain Text
 
x-csrf-token|Cookie

Question

  1. Is this the correct approach for manually handling CSRF tokens in CPI HTTP Adapter?

  2. Is it mandatory to pass the cookies returned in set-cookie as a request header named Cookie for ABAP OData V4 services?

  3. Has anyone successfully implemented GET (Fetch CSRF) + POST using HTTP Adapter against an ABAP OData V4 endpoint?

  4. Is there a better CPI-native way to preserve the HTTP session between the GET and POST calls?

Any guidance or working example would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance!

entry.title: Avoiding Order Lock Conflicts in S/4HANA During Concurrent Updates from CPI
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

I would like to seek your advice on handling order lock conflicts in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud during updates from SAP CPI.

Our scenario is as follows:

  • An external system sends multiple messages for the same order in separate transactions.
  • SAP CPI processes each message independently and updates the corresponding order in S/4HANA Public Cloud.
  • While the first message is still processing and updating the order, a second message for the same order arrives and attempts another update.
  • Since the order is still being processed by the first transaction, it is locked in S/4HANA Public Cloud, causing the second message to fail with a lock-related error.

Has anyone encountered a similar situation? What approaches or best practices would you recommend to prevent or handle these order lock conflicts?

For example:

  • Is there a way to queue or serialize updates for the same order?
  • Are there standard SAP patterns for managing concurrent updates to the same business object?

Any guidance or recommendations would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you!

#sapcpi #sapintegrationsuite

entry.title: RateLimit headers visible in adapter trace but not propagated to next CPI components
entry.content:
Hi Team,
 
As part of SAP SuccessFactors API Rate Limiting Enhancements introduced with the 2608 release, SAP recommends that customers start monitoring and logging the RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy response headers in their middleware or API clients.
 
According to SAP documentation (API Rate Limiting Enhancements and Guardrails), all applicable API responses now contain:
 
- RateLimit-Policy
- RateLimit
 
We tried to log these headers in our integration flows, however in the trace information for the component immediately following the SuccessFactors receiver adapter, these headers are no longer available for us to log through the groovy script.
